long_biography.plain_text:
Rifaat al-Assad's command of Syria's Defense Brigades placed him at the centre of the Assad security state. The force took part in the 1982 Hama assault, which killed thousands. Swiss prosecutors later indicted him for alleged war crimes and crimes against humanity, but his death ended the proceedings without a judgment.

After a failed challenge to his brother Hafez, Assad spent most of his exile in France and Spain, acquiring a substantial European property portfolio. French courts convicted him of laundering diverted Syrian state funds and imposed a four-year prison sentence; the Cour de cassation made the conviction and confiscation final in 2022. He returned to Syria before the final appeal and fled again after Bashar al-Assad's government fell.
